comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
I think this is a security measure in recent Debians. IMO the correct way to add the key is following:
1. Download grafana repo key and dearmor it. `cat grafana.key | gpg --dearmor > grafana.gpg`
2. Copy `grafana.gpg` into `/etc/apt/keyrings`. In releases older than Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04, `/etc/apt/keyrings` does not exist by default. It SHOULD be created with permissions 0755 if it is needed and does not already exist.
3. Update `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/grafana.list` and paste following:
```
deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/grafana.gpg] https://<redacted-host> stable main
```
More info: https://wiki.debian.org/DebianRepository/UseThirdParty

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Got it working now, the culprit seemed to be a permission problem on the /etc/apt/keyrings directory even that everybody had read on the directory a regular user was not able to read the grafana.gpg key file. 

A rename of the problematic directory and then creating it again and moving the grafana.gpg file back made it work

Thank you for the help, I'm not sure I had found that one myself.
